div.div:
con-sĕpĕlĭo , no
I.perf., sepultus, 4, v. a., to bury with: “consepeliri cum aliquo,” Ambros. in Luc. 6, 7, § 30 : corporis morti consepeliri in baptismo. Hil. Trin. 1, p. 3.— Perf. part.: consĕpultus , buried with, Tert. Res. Carn. 23; Hier. Ep. 14, n. 2 al.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
